newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Storms over Caspian delay Kazakh-Iranian oil swaps.
newsitem.headline: Storms over Caspian delay Kazakh-Iranian oil swaps.

text.p: An oil exchange deal between Kazakhstan and Iran is being delayed until the end of January because of stormy weather over the Caspian Sea, Russia's Interfax news agency quoted a Kazakh official as saying on Wednesday.

Boris Pak, deputy head of the former Soviet republic's state-owned oil trader Munayimpex, told Interfax that the first tanker with Kazakh oil reached the Iranian shore on December 31 to test the future route.
"We have realised the transport scheme is reliable," Pak told the agency.
The deal was agreed in Tehran last month and officials have said volumes could eventually reach 6 million tonnes.
Kazakhstan would ship its oil across the Caspian Sea to Iran's Caspian Sea coast. In turn, Iran would provide the equivalent amount of crude at its Gulf ports.
The United States, which has imposed sanctions against Iran saying the country sponsors terrorism, views the deal with concern as some of its own oil majors are investing in Kazakh oil projects.
Kazakhstan has said that only state-owned oil, and not output from Western companies, will be part of the swaps.
The Central Asian country is anxious to break its reliance on neighbouring Russia to the north for oil exports.
